title: High Throughput Pipette-Tip Hydroponics for Collecting Salt Stress Samples for RNA-seq
author: Magdalena M Julkowska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bazeif3e

steps.title: Sterilize Arabidopsis seeds
steps.instruction: Place up to ±400 Arabidopsis seeds in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube, add 1 mL of 50 % household bleach (diluted with sterile MQ water), and incubate for 10–20 min.

steps.title: Wash sterilized seeds
steps.instruction: Rinse the seeds with 2 mL sterile MQ water 5–8 times, preferably inside a laminar flow hood.

steps.title: Cold‑stratify seeds
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed seeds in MQ water, keep them in the dark at 4 °C for at least overnight but no longer than one week to break dormancy.

steps.title: Cut pipette‑tip studs
steps.instruction: Using large, sturdy scissors, cut the yellow 1 mL pipette tip so that only the wider stud (the bottom portion) remains; this stud will be used as the hydroponic chamber.

steps.title: Prepare solid agar medium
steps.instruction: For 1 L, dissolve 2.2 g Murashige‑Skoog nutrients and 1 g MES buffer in water, adjust pH to 5.8 with KOH, then add 10 g Dashin agar. Autoclave or melt in a microwave. Store at room temperature (≈2 weeks) or at 65 °C (up to 3 days). Warm in a microwave before use to keep liquid.

steps.title: Fill pipette studs with agar (bottom)
steps.instruction: Place each cut pipette stud into a clean PCR plate, add liquid agar medium just enough to cover the bottom part, and allow it to solidify.

steps.title: Fill pipette studs to full height
steps.instruction: After the bottom agar has solidified, add more liquid agar to fill the entire length of the stud, forming a meniscus rather than a bulb to facilitate seed placement.

steps.title: Prepare liquid nutrient solution
steps.instruction: For 1 L, dissolve 2.2 g Murashige‑Skoog nutrients and 1 g MES buffer, adjust pH to 5.8 with KOH. Autoclaving is optional unless required for a specific reason.

steps.title: Assemble hydroponic boxes
steps.instruction: Insert the agar‑filled pipette studs into a 1 mL tip box, positioning them deeper than in a standard “yellow tip box”. Fill the box with the liquid nutrient solution until the medium level is just below the plate holding the studs (not covering them completely).

steps.title: Place seeds on agar and incubate
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette tip, drop the cold‑treated seeds onto the surface of the agar in each stud. Seal the box with its transparent lid and place it in a growth chamber set to 18 °C, 12 h light/12 h dark cycle, 60 % humidity.

steps.title: Monitor media and thin seedlings
steps.instruction: Check the liquid media level daily and replace the entire medium every 5–7 days. Four days after box placement, germination should be visible; thin seedlings so that only one seedling remains per agar stud.

steps.title: Allow root emergence
steps.instruction: Between 1–2 weeks after germination, roots will grow out of the agar studs. Keep the liquid level just below the stud plate to avoid submerging the studs completely.

steps.title: Transfer to larger hydroponics
steps.instruction: At two weeks of growth, move the seedlings to larger hydroponic containers containing 2 L of the same liquid nutrient solution per container.

steps.title: Apply salt stress and harvest
steps.instruction: When replacing the medium at three weeks after germination, add 100 mM NaCl to the liquid nutrient solution. Harvest shoot and root tissues into separate tubes for RNA isolation. (Salt stress can be applied earlier, as soon as roots exit the agar stud.)
